title: Fractional wheel deltas never zoom — the PR's claimed per-frame accumulation does not exist
detail: i32(delta) truncates sub-notch deltas to zero and nothing accumulates remainders across frames; slow trackpad scrolling (e.g. 0.25/frame) yields identity zoom steps forever — the accumulation claim is unimplemented.
recommended_fix: Accumulate the fractional wheel remainder (in the poll or the effect) and fire a whole-notch zoom only when the accumulated magnitude reaches 1.

title: Pan latch strands while the pan branch is suppressed; the missed-release guard then synthesizes a Mouse_Release every frame
detail: The guard's synthesized release only clears `panning` inside the pan branch, which `panel_open` suppresses; a settings-modal key mid-drag strands the latch, emitting releases every frame, then a stale-anchored Pan jump plus spurious Select on close.
recommended_fix: Clear inp.panning directly in the poll guard (or when the modal opens) instead of relying on the suppressed pan branch to consume the synthesized release.

title: effect_pan converts screen deltas at the target zoom, not the "live scale" the hook comments promise
evidence:
+		nx, ny := rnd.camera_pan_center(app.cam_wx_to, app.cam_wy_to, dx, dy, fit, app.cam_zoom_to)
---
+		// routes to the app's on_pan effect (world units against the live
+		// scale + the world-rect clamp). The parity harness leaves the hook
detail: Both hook comments say deltas convert "against the live scale", but effect_pan passes cam_zoom_to; mid-ease pans mis-scale until the camera converges.
recommended_fix: Convert at the live eased scale, or reword both comments to say target scale so documented behavior matches the math.

title: Clamp-test comment claims x is free at fit while the assertion (correctly) pins x to the world center
evidence:
+	// at the fit (z=1) the viewport is larger than the world in x? no — the
+	// world is 1040 wide vs the 960px viewport, so x is free; y (720 viewport
+	// vs 780 world) pins. At z < 1.08 both pin. The min-zoom contract: the
+	// fit is the OUT limit, so the fit center is the world center.
---
+	cx, cy := camera_clamp_center(9999, -9999, win_w, win_h, FIT42, 1.0, WORLD_W42, WORLD_H42)
+	testing.expect(t, abs(cx - WORLD_W42 / 2) < TOL && abs(cy - WORLD_H42 / 2) < TOL, "fit clamps to the world center")
detail: At fit, half_w = 640/0.923 ≈ 693 ≥ 520, so x pins — the assertion is right; the comment's "x is free" reasoning and its "960px viewport" figure are wrong.
recommended_fix: Fix the comment: at fit both axes pin (the 1280×720 window exceeds the 960×720 scaled world); keep the assertion as is.

title: PP_CAM_E2E env string is never freed and any non-empty value (even "0") enables the drive
detail: The heap-allocated env string is discarded without freeing, and the != "" check treats PP_CAM_E2E=0 as enabled.
recommended_fix: Use a non-allocating existence check (or free the string) and treat "0"/"false" as disabled.

title: camera_fit's "ONE source" comment is false — the diff adds a third copy of the fit formula
detail: The comment itself admits the same derivation already exists in view_compute and camera_update; the diff adds a re-derivation instead of unifying them.
recommended_fix: Hoist the fit derivation into one render-package helper called by view_compute, camera_update, and camera_fit.
